name: PayPal
description: PayPal runs a two-sided payments network: 439 million active accounts (consumers and merchants) across about 200 markets. It earns a fee on each payment, and 90 percent of revenue is these transaction fees, charged to merchants and consumers, across PayPal checkout, Venmo, Xoom and Braintree (card processing for large merchants). The remaining 10 percent is other value added services: interest and fees on its own loans, a revenue share from a partner bank on PayPal-branded credit, referral and subscription fees. The 10-K says transaction revenue grew slower than payment volume in 2025 because of product and merchant mix and hedging, and that it is shifting Braintree toward profitable volume (fewer transactions, more volume). It pays a quarterly dividend, started in October 2025, and buys back stock heavily.

businessLines.name: Transaction revenues
businessLines.how: A percentage-plus-fixed fee on each payment, charged to merchants and consumers; revenue rises with total payment volume, transaction count and cross-border mix, and falls when merchants negotiate or mix shifts to lower-priced Braintree volume.
businessLines.description: Net transaction fees charged to merchants and consumers on payment volume completed on the platform: PayPal and Venmo checkout and P2P, Braintree, Xoom.

businessLines.name: Revenues from other value added services
businessLines.how: Interest and fees on loans PayPal keeps on its balance sheet, plus a revenue share from a partner bank that funds PayPal-branded credit (zero in a quarter if that credit programme misses its minimum return), plus referral and subscription fees.
businessLines.description: Interest and fees on loans receivable, revenue share from a partner institution on PayPal-branded credit, referral and partnership revenue, subscription and gateway fees.
